answer: Progressive identity pricing blunts Sybil attacks in an agent economy. A first identity costs one small fee, but each extra identity from the same wallet or attestation cluster costs double the last, so the summit of the fee curve climbs fast: fielding a hundred sock puppets costs a fortune, while one honest agent pays almost nothing. Fees are burned, never refunded. Every identity carries a beacon recording its cluster, so the network spots clusters forming. Honest agents register once and build reputation; an attacker carving a karst of hollow identities pays a rising toll per extra face.
